curriculum.lesson_evidence: In challenge games a team works on a task that is hard at first, such as passing a beanbag around a circle without dropping it. Persisting together means encouraging teammates, changing the plan after a mistake and celebrating improvement. Kind encouragement names a specific effort, like 'good recovery'. Games must be safe, with soft equipment and enough space, and everyone chooses their own level.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A team drops the beanbag three times in a row and one player says, 'This is pointless.' Write a kind response and one change to the plan.

FEEDBACK
Response: 'We got 4 passes that time, let's call names first.' Change: pass more slowly, throw softer or stand closer. Naming what improved and changing one part of the plan keeps everyone included.

WATCH FOR
Thinking persisting means keeping going with an unsafe or unfair game. Persisting means working at the challenge in a safe, kind way; teams stop and change the rules if someone is unsafe or left out.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Invent a challenge game for 2 to 4 players using soft equipment (rolled-up socks or a cushion). Write the goal, the safety rules, an easy and a hard version and three encouraging sentences. Play it and record the team's best score in each round.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
